result:
All three solutions give the same count, $\binom{N+1}{3}=\frac{(N-1)N(N+1)}{6}$. Each assumes that distinct sorted triples $(a_1,a_2,a_3)$ give non-isomorphic surfaces, so the count is the number of multisets of size 3 from $\{2,\dots,N\}$.

I did not prove this assumption. It matches my recollection that Pham–Brieskorn surfaces $x_1^{a_1}+x_2^{a_2}+x_3^{a_3}+1=0$ are isomorphic only when their exponents agree up to permutation, but I could not confirm a specific published theorem here. The invariants the solutions cite (Milnor number, the link at infinity, log Kodaira dimension) are plausible, and the spot checks of small cases look consistent.

Since the three final answers are equivalent, I pick Solution 1, whose final line is cleanly written.

CHOICE: 1
